DM: You smash them up good!
DM: Dumb, not like me. I'm not dumb.
DM: Yeah, he taps the rock. Good rock.

Kenzo: Alright, I think we've learned what we need to learn. It was great. We're gonna save that one. Yeah, that one—that ogre is not gonna die. Okay, so we thank, we thank the ogre. We, we work—we tell them to get excited for when we, when the rock throws itself at the [garbled].
DM: Have you heard enough, Rock?

DM: Do I get my...? Do I get my whatever it is you promised me? I don't remember now.

DM: That's a stupid question. Never scared. There's a story somebody told me...
Kenzo: Hmm. Tell me the story. Yeah.

DM: Tell him no good. Big man, big, big boss man the best.

before: DM: Everybody who, who brings the special rocks to Dhrukmir is rewarded. The, the people who bring the most special rocks get the whips the next day, and they get a day off, and the people who bring the least special rocks, well, you don't want to be one of those people.

interactions.title: The singing giant discovers the hidden party
lines: DM: The sun sets, and it begins to get dark, and about an hour after, you know, half an hour after sunset, you hear a sort of quiet, very deep bass voice singing what sounds like a some kind of song in, in Giantish, and it's, it's sort of a—it's like a, you know, epic poem style set, set to a sort of bass chant that is, that is telling a story about how the mountains were created. This seems like a legend or some sort of stone giant tale about how the giant—the mountains were sculpted by their All-Father, and it, you know, it's, it's, it's...

DM: The, the idea is it's kind of, it's just kind of a sort of an ancient tale, and he seems to be humming it under his, under his breath a little bit and kind of waiting after each stanza to hear if there's a reply.
Delwath: Delwath will attempt to echo a verse back.
Delwath: All right, I'll do it in Elvish.
DM: ((Performance assistance)) the song pauses, and the giant turns and looks back at the rock and walks over and looks behind that, because he's way taller than the rock.

DM: He speaks in halting Common. I have not heard that tongue in hundreds of years. What are one of the forest people doing in this place? Why are you singing to me? I would flee if I were you before you die.

Kenzo: Kenzo will speak directly in Giant. But hello, friend! We are, we are, we are friends. I know this is, might be a surprise to see such beings as us here, but perhaps our interests in this area are aligned, and that way we may be able to help you.
DM: He's, like, bending way, way down, leaning over and, like, puts his hands, reaches down and and picks up Kenzo. “Say that again. Talk quietly, please,” holding you next to his ear.
Kenzo: We, we may very well be friends, and we may be able to help you in your situation here.
Kenzo: The giant that lives in the pit, is he your friend or your foe?
DM: An abomination against all that giants stand for.
Kenzo: Then we are aligned. Would you like to see him out of this valley?
DM: He puts you down on top of the rock. We are not aligned. You may have common interests.

DM: He looks at the 4 of you. You obviously are not weak if you've made it past the chalyte eyes without alerting the guard, and you have done some mind magic to that poor dumb creature, and you're obviously clever.
DM: He, like, picks up the boulder and, like, shifts a little bit out of the way and then sits down. I'm not sure what you think you are attempting to accomplish here.

Delwath: It. It seems to us that if, and we knew more of the workings of that
Delwath: and if it was disabled,

DM: I will not... It stops. We'll have to think.

DM: Not everybody is happy with this state of affairs. But there are only 2 fates for those who express their displeasure: disintegration or slowly being used up by the lightning until turn into something unrecognizable, burned out husk of a creature.
Kenzo: Choose freedom. That's what we offer.
Delwath: Well, if we can find a way to destroy that thing,
Delwath: take its power away, we think freedom is within your grasp.

DM: You must be careful, for thunder booms constantly within it. It's distracting and hard to focus, and the husks left behind by those of my people who have died at the hands of the abomination will fight you, and some of the traitors who have sought to worship this false god also study the secrets of this false power, this frozen magic that is not even a true stone, not a real gemstone at all.

DM: So it is not, it is not a place that where you will find ease and comfort, and I must presume you have some way of reaching it, flight or magic, for I do not think, unless you are immune to the deadly forces of lightning, which most of us are, you'll not be able to use the normal way of transport, allowing yourself to be carried by the lightning burst.

interactions.title: How the weapon is powered and why escape is dangerous
lines: DM: So he also says nobody knows exactly what the abomination did to construct it, but I am confident that those of your obvious prowess can find a way to at least disrupt the flow of energy that powers the thing, if not destroy it outright. You can see where the energy flows from the chalyte, and he sort of makes a bitter face as if he doesn't even like saying that word, in the mountains, through—is pointing up—the arcane bolts and down through the middle of the thing to charge the destruction that can be unleashed. Just needs to be blocked somehow.
Wellby: Can the beam target the tower?
DM: The one place in this valley that is safe from the beam is the inside of the tower. But be warned: once the abomination has seen you, he can target you anywhere within a day's walk.

DM: My brother snuck out at night many years ago, after a sculpture carved into the side of the mountain he had worked—was getting mad—for a hundred years to produce was carelessly smashed to power that thing. That... But 2 days later they carried his ashes back. Must have gotten 15 miles away in the night at least.
DM: Says, but if you can get inside the tower unseen,
DM: and what, there's a lot you might be able to do.
Kenzo: What do we do once we're inside?
Delwath: We block the flow of energy to the thing, right?
Kenzo: I'm asking the giant, but, like...
Delwath: That's what he told us.
Kenzo: That's what he just said. Block the flow of energy, or...
DM: He looks at the 4 of you. Someone with more arcane knowledge than me may be able to figure out a way to destroy it completely at the source.

before: DM: It might just crash!

lines: DM: Yes, so to wrap up the conversation with the giant before we call it quits for tonight, so he, you talk a little bit more, and he, you know, he talks about again how, you know, clearly warming up to you and sort of wondering, oh, maybe they'll actually pull it off.

DM: And he's not willing to, he's not willing to fight, but there's a group of, of a group of these—of giants that, like, half or more that, he said, want to leave, who are at least willing to break the—knock down the road.
DM: So the ogres are trapped in the pit.
Kenzo: Any other things that he can do that are the equivalent of, like, tying the shoelaces of the dude before he stays? You know any things like that.
DM: Yeah, no, he’s like, once 50 foot abomination starts climbing out of his pit, we’re running. That will, like...
Kenzo: Totally fine, but sabotage as much as we can beforehand. That’s cool, but also is there any...
Delwath: Other giants... My only real concern is that while we're killing 50 foot abomination, we get swarmed by 6 giants, and we can't take 6 giants and 50 foot abomination.
Delwath: We want him to try and, like...
Kenzo: Can, can you help us with enough distraction so that we can focus on the abomination, and then think on it?
DM: Yeah, he's—he says, I'll think on it.
DM: It says, the one—the ones they're scared, the ones that they're scared of are the chalyte sorcerers.

DM: If those... He does not think anybody is going to challenge a chalyte sorcerer, but he's pretty sure that it, 2 of them, one or 2 of them, always are in the tower, anyway, and you're pretty sure that there's only 2 chalyte sorcerers.
Delwath: Oh, okay, so we might kill the chalyte sorcerers on our way through the tower, and then...
DM: Or you might have to deal with one chalyte sorcerer while you're dealing with the abomination. But he's—he says, though, he'll do his—can guarantee, destroy the road. Ogres will be trapped.

DM: The other thing that he says is that Dhrukmir does not emerge often, and when he does it is slow. You hear the echoes and the thunder, like 10 min before he begins to grow out of pits below, where he...
Kenzo: Lives, and insists on being worshipped. Are the pits...?
DM: No, nobody—I mean, the ogres go in the mines. The abomination, the Dhrukmir, lives down there somewhere, but the giants don't go down.
DM: But he's saying, when you hear the, like, booming thunder from below, you have about 10 min before you have to face the abomination.

lines: DM: When you teleport—so when you teleport to this, to... It is about 40 miles away.
DM: Faldrak has spent most of the time that you were walking flying away from the death ray.
DM: And you say smart, and he's like, “I knew it. I knew you didn't want me to stay close to the death ray.”
